findings.description: The DB username and password are interpolated into EC2 user data and written to a local PHP configuration file. This exposes the credential through Terraform state and to principals or processes able to retrieve instance user data or read the file.

The RDS instance explicitly sets publicly_accessible = true, causing AWS to provision a public endpoint/addressing path. Its currently shown ingress is limited to the VPC CIDR, but the public exposure is still an unnecessary externally routable database configuration and enlarges the impact of any permissive security-group change.
storage_encrypted is explicitly set to false, so RDS database storage, automated backups, read replicas, and snapshots created from this instance are not encrypted at rest.

The policy grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on every resource to a role attached to the application EC2 instance. Compromise of that instance can therefore provide broad control over these services, including destructive actions and potential IAM-adjacent privilege-escalation paths through EC2 and service resource manipulation.
